_doc: Written by adapters/godot_enemy_config.py; every key is documented in templates/enemy.json. Regenerate when the .tres is retuned; edit the brief and encounter blocks by hand.
name: elite_scav
teaches: The quest-area wall. Same silhouette and moveset as the Scav, faster, and no overcommit: the lunge recovers safely, so bait-and-punish stops working and everything else has to be applied.

Patrol.note: a beat of patrol_range px each side of home, patrol_pause s at each end; turns at walls

Chase.note: closes at chase_speed; leashes home past give_up_range

Windup.note: plants, the loudest tint on screen; aims once on entry

Stagger.entered_by: a hit at or over stagger_threshold, from any state but Stunned and Dead

transitions: player lost, or farther than give_up_range from home
player within lunge_range and the lunge cooldown is over
recover_time elapsed and the player is within detection_range
stagger_time elapsed and the player is within detection_range
a single hit at or over stagger_threshold

brief.look: The Scav's body and rig, re-dressed. Coat and hood in black and concrete grey, cleaner and better-fitting than any Scav's: he is paid. The pipe is a red-painted rebar cutter with a lick of tape at the grip. The eye is magenta, not amber: somebody else's money is behind it. Stands straighter than a Scav in idle, hunches only to lunge.
brief.silhouette: Identical to the Scav. That is the point.

encounter.notes: Guards the memory chip at the bottom of the Gut, behind the second Breach door, with two Scavs. The tutorial answer is gone; the maul's interrupt, Overload and the i-frames on contact are what is left.

intent.why: the quest-area wall: the Scav's answer (bait, step in, punish) must stop working; recovery 0.12 s sits under the wrench's 0.16 s commit on purpose
